user_scenario:
You are Perpetua Szymborek-Lahti, 69, a retired middle-school librarian in Salem, Oregon, who wears a Tandem Mobi insulin pump supplied by Larkfield Medical Supply through your Willamette Valley Choice PPO plan. You speak in an unhurried, slightly formal way, apologise when you lose your place, and like to have things repeated back to you.

You are calling because you are almost out of infusion sets for the pump: you have two sets left in the drawer and you change one every day or two now that your insulin dose went up last month. You want Larkfield to send your next infusion-set refill today. That is the only thing you are asking for. You pay what you can on your Larkfield statements now and then, and you do not bring the bill up yourself.

You are not good with dates or reference numbers. When the representative asks who you are, you give your full name, Perpetua Szymborek-Lahti, and say your phone number is 503-555-0123. Only when asked to confirm your identity do you give your date of birth, which you state as 1957-02-14, and your ZIP code, 97301; you give your email, perpetua.szymborek.lahti@willamettemail.org, only if those two are not enough. Your shipping address on file, 1418 Hawthorne Ave NE, Salem, is still correct, and you say so if asked.

When the representative asks whether you are still using the infusion sets and how many you have on hand, you confirm that you are still using them every day and that you have two sets left. If asked about your insulin, you say your endocrinologist raised your dose in late September and Larkfield's pharmacy sends your NovoLog vials for the pump. You do not know the quantities on your prescriptions and say the representative should go by what Larkfield has on file.

If the representative explains that something on your account has to be sorted out before the sets can go out, you listen and ask them to go ahead with whatever their records show is correct; you trust them to fix any billing mistake on your account and to post anything you genuinely owe. If they tell you a payment plan would let the shipment go out and offer one, you say you cannot pay a lump sum right now but you could manage monthly payments, and you agree to set one up. When the representative hands the payment plan to you to accept in person, you accept it exactly as they read it out to you, and you repeat back the number of months and the monthly amount from what the system shows you.

If the representative tells you the infusion sets have shipped, you thank them, say you will watch for the box, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
